text: Sadia Qadir, a medical sales officer with a declared monthly income of PKR 150,000, has exhibited a pattern of structuring cash deposits to evade reporting thresholds. Between July 6 and July 28, 2026, she made 14 separate cash deposits totaling approximately PKR 24.3 million across four different branches in Karachi (Clifton, Gulshan-e-Iqbal, DHA Phase 6, and Saddar). Each deposit was kept just below the PKR 2 million Cash Transaction Report (CTR) threshold, ranging from PKR 956,000 to PKR 1,993,000. This activity is highly inconsistent with her declared salary and occupation. Following these deposits, she made large outgoing transfers to three counterparties: Sheraz Traders (PKR 7,069,000 total), Crescent Imports (PKR 6,970,000 total), and Al-Noor Exchange Company (PKR 5,866,000 total). The rapid movement of funds from cash deposits to third-party accounts, combined with the deliberate avoidance of CTR limits through multiple branch usage, strongly suggests money laundering or the layering of illicit funds. The involvement of an exchange company further heightens the risk of currency conversion for illicit purposes. This behavior warrants a Suspicious Transaction Report.
